name: Ghamoo-ra
summary: In Blackfathom Deeps, Ghamoo-ra guards a small island in the Pool of Ask'ar. The ancient giant turtle tramples anyone who draws near.

sections.title: A Beast of the Drowned Temple
sections.body: Blackfathom Deeps was once a night elven temple to Elune. Now flooded, its ruins belong to naga, satyr, and the nihilistic Twilight's Hammer cult. Ghamoo-ra dwells among them, his enormous, thick shell turning aside all but the strongest blows.

sections.title: Guardian of the Deeps
sections.body: Lesser turtles gather around Ghamoo-ra on a small island in the Pool of Ask'ar, yet they leave travelers alone. Ghamoo-ra attacks anyone who comes near. Beneath his trampling bulk, they are crushed.

faq.answer: Ghamoo-ra guards a small island in the Pool of Ask'ar, within Blackfathom Deeps. The flooded temple of Elune is held by the Twilight's Hammer, and Ghamoo-ra attacks anyone who approaches.

faq.q: Why is Ghamoo-ra hostile to outsiders?
faq.answer: Nothing is recorded of how Ghamoo-ra grew so savage. He attacks anyone who intrudes on his island in the Pool of Ask'ar, trampling all who come near.
Yes. Though Ghamoo-ra is large and has endured years of torment, a skilled hunter can tame him.

faq.q: What is the Pool of Ask'ar?
faq.answer: The Pool of Ask'ar is a flooded cavern beneath Blackfathom Deeps. Ghamoo-ra roams the center of a small island there, among docile native turtles.

faq.q: What connection does he have to the Old Gods?
faq.answer: None is recorded. Ghamoo-ra is a beast of the deep, while Twilight's Hammer cultists who worship the Old Gods have overrun the sunken temple around him.

angles.text: As a hunter venturing into Blackfathom Deeps, you may pity Ghamoo-ra, an ancient beast of the deep. With patience, you may tame him.
As a night elf, you may see Ghamoo-ra's savage presence in Elune's drowned temple as a bitter reminder of how far the sacred site has fallen to the vile Twilight's Hammer.
As a druid, you find in Ghamoo-ra an ancient creature of the deep, grown savage amid the ruins of the defiled temple.
